# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

We only provide security updates for the latest tagged version (by date).

Security issues are only within scope when the software is used in a supported environment and for the intended purpose, and only as long as the issue arises from our code – not the Operating System, not the programming language, not the site or third party service you are connecting to.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

> [!CAUTION]
> Do NOT report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub Issues or any other form of _public_ communication.

Please use GitHub Security Advisories to report vulnerabilities.

1. Go to the [Security tab](https://github.com/grafida/grafida/security/advisories).
2. Click "Report a vulnerability".
3. Fill out the advisory form.

This creates a private discussion visible only to the maintainer.

## Response Timeline

Realistic commitments we can actually meet:

- **Initial response**: Within 4 business days
- **Status update**: Within 14 business days
- **Resolution target**: Within 90 days

Regarding the resolution target, we generally aim for fast resolution, ideally a single-digit number of days. If we propose a timeline which is too short for you, please do tell us.

Kindly note that the resolution target does not include the amount of time it takes Google to review the new version and release it.

### What to do if you do not receive a timely reply.

This is a single-person company. The availability of the developer may be limited due to factors outside his control such as illness or family obligations. We are unlikely to be out of contact for more than five days.

If you do not receive an initial response within 10 calendar days, please try contacting us again. A simple "Bump" comment on your vulnerability report is enough.

If you do not receive an answer after 30 calendar days, please check our site's public tickets. If there is activity, please do try to contact us using a public support ticket in the Pre-sales category, asking us for further steps.

If, however, you see no activity from us in the public tickets in the past 30 days, our lead developer is probably deathly ill, or dead – that, too, is part of life. We do have a plan in place, having set up our spouse as a legacy contact. However, we doubt that “unpublish GitHub repositories and unpublish the site” would be their top priority in this eventuality. In the unlikely event this unfortunate sequence of events takes place, we merely ask you to follow your conscience.

## Disclosure Policy

- **Coordinated disclosure**: We work with reporters to agree on a disclosure timeline.
- **Credit**: Security reporters are credited in release notes and advisories (unless they prefer anonymity).
- **CVE assignment**: We request CVEs through GitHub for verified vulnerabilities; due to the nature of this process, we may not have a CVE number when we publish a security update.

## Use of generative AI

We find AI-powered code assistants to be very useful development tools, especially in discovering and addressing security issues. However, the very nature of these tools leaves a great margin for error and misuse. If you are using AI to discover and / or report security issues, we ask you to heed the following ground rules.

**Mark your submissions with `[AI]`** if you used generative AI for anything other than translation or proofreading.

**No laundry list of unverified claims**. We run AI-assisted security audits using various frontier models with regularity. We have already seen the same report you are about to send us. Please don't.

**Only run it against the working copy, having installed the dependencies**. Do NOT run a code assistant against the distributed binary, or the source code ZIP file generated by GitHub. It will lack important context, leading to invalid results.

**Make sure it is reproducible**. Generative AI often hallucinates impossible issues. Ask it to create a Proof-of-Concept (POC). If it fails or produces something working, it was never a real issue.

**Check if it's a valid issue**. Generative AI does not understand who, when, where, or how will be using this software. It's your responsibility to take that into account.

**Answer follow-up questions**. If you are not willing to do that, please don't report an issue.

**You are ultimately responsible for your submission**. When you submit a bug or security issue report to our repositories, you take full credit _and_ full responsibility for it. With great power comes great responsibility.

## Bug Bounty

As a tiny, single-person company with very limited resources, we regrettably cannot and do not offer a bug bounty program. Security reports are greatly appreciated and credited. Thank you for helping keep everyone safe!
